facts.statement: The species Palintropus retusus is known from a proximal coracoid found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
facts.quote: A single species has been named (Palintropus retusus) based on a proximal coracoid from the Lance Formation of Wyoming, dated to the latest Maastrichtian, million years ago.

facts.statement: The type species Palintropus retusus is based on a proximal coracoid from the Lance Formation of Wyoming dated to 65.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce una especie, Palintropus retusus, basada en un coracoides proximal hallado en la Formación Lance de Wyoming, en Estados Unidos, que data de finales del Maastrichtiense, hace 65.5 millones de años.

facts.statement: Unnamed species from the Campanian of Alberta are represented by coracoids and a proximal scapula dating to between 76.5 and 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: También se han hallado restos de coracoides y una escápula proximal de dos especies sin nombrar de la Formación Dinosaur Park de Alberta, Canadá, que data de entre 76.5 a 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense.

facts.statement: The genus was initially placed in the wastebin genus Cimolopteryx.
facts.quote: Este inicialmente fue situado en el género taxón cajón de sastre "Cimolopteryx".

facts.statement: Pierce Brodkorb assigned the current name in 1970, after first affiliating it with Apatornis in 1963.
facts.quote: Pierce Brodkorb le asignó su nombre actual, primero incluyéndolo en el género Apatornis en 1963, y luego estableciendo su propio nombre de género en 1970.

facts.statement: Some researchers believe Palintropus is an early member of the Charadriiformes, similar to birds of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: Like many of the birds of the subtropical coastlands of the Western Interior Seaway - maybe a bit like eastern Australia today - it is sometimes believed to be an early member of the Charadriiformes (waders, gulls, auks, etc.; see also "Graculavidae").

facts.statement: An alternate theory suggests Palintropus is a galliform, possibly a quercymegapodiid.
facts.quote: However, an alternate theory is that it is a galliform, perhaps a quercymegapodiid.

facts.statement: A 2009 cladistic analysis by Longrich and colleagues suggested Palintropus is a primitive bird related to Apsaravis and belongs in the family Palintropiformes.
facts.quote: In 2009, Longrich and colleagues proposed that Palintropus is a primitive bird related to Apsaravis. They conducted the first cladistic analysis of the remains, and found this to be the most likely hypothesis, suggesting Palintropus warrants inclusion in the newly established Palintropiformes.

facts.statement: In 2011, Longrich and colleagues proposed that Palintropus is a primitive bird related to Apsaravis.
facts.quote: En 2011, Longrich et al. propusieron que Palintropus es un ave primitiva relacionada con Apsaravis.

facts.statement: The first cladistic analysis determined that Palintropus likely belongs to the newly established group Palintropiformes.
facts.quote: Ellos llevaron a cabo el primer análisis cladístico de los restos, y determinaron que esa es la hipótesis más probable, sugiriendo que esto garantiza la inclusión de Palintropus en el grupo recientemente establecido Palintropiformes.

facts.statement: The relationships of Palintropus are poorly determined mainly due to the scarcity of material.
facts.quote: Sus relaciones no están bien determinadas, mayormente debido a la escasez del material.

facts.statement: It is sometimes believed to be a primitive member of the Charadriiformes order, similar to birds of the subtropical coastlands of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: Varias ideas se han propuesto: como muchas aves de las tierras costeras subtropicales del Mar de Niobrara - tal vez similar a la actual Australia oriental - se cree que era un miembro primitivo del orden de las Charadriiformes (aves zancudas, gaviotas, alcas, etc.; véase también "Graculavidae").

facts.statement: An alternative theory is that it is a Galliforme, perhaps a quercymegapodiid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la teoría alternativa es que se trata de un Galliforme, quizás un quercymegapódido.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Palintropus as Quercymegapodiidae.
The family assigned to Palintropus in the Paleobiology Database is Quercymegapodiidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Palintropus under the class Reptilia.
The time range for Palintropus is recorded as Campanian to Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Remains of two unnamed species, including coracoids and a proximal scapula, date to between 76.5 and 75 million years ago from the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta.
rejected.quote: Coracoids and a proximal scapula of two unnamed species from the upper Campanian Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, dating to between 76.5 and 75 million years ago, are also known.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'to between 76.5 and 75 million years ago'
